simpson-2017.title: Calorie counting and fitness tracking technology: Associations with eating disorder symptomatology
simpson-2017.support: 493 college students; calorie tracker users showed higher eating concern and dietary restraint.

gibson-2016.title: Accuracy of handsv. household measures as portion size estimation aids
gibson-2016.support: 67 participants estimated 42 pre-weighed foods; 80% of geometric foods estimated with the finger width method were within 25% of true weight and 13% within 10%, vs 29% within 25% for household measures.

helms-2019.title: Towards a Sustainable Nutrition Paradigm in Physique Sport: A Narrative Review
helms-2019.support: Tentative best-practice recommendations include dietary flexibility, slower weight loss and structured monitoring.

odriscoll-2020.title: How well do activity monitors estimate energy expenditure? A systematic review and meta-analysis of the validity of current technologies
odriscoll-2020.support: 60 studies (104 effect sizes); devices showed variable accuracy depending on activity type, with large heterogeneity.

hultman-1996.title: Muscle creatine loading in men
hultman-1996.support: Muscle total creatine concentration increased by approximately 20% after 6 days of creatine supplementation at a rate of 20 g/day. ... A similar, but more gradual, 20% increase in muscle total creatine concentration was observed over a period of 28 days when supplementation was undertaken at a rate of 3 g/day.

goldstein-2010.title: International society of sports nutrition position stand: caffeine and performance
goldstein-2010.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
goldstein-2010.support: Caffeine is effective for enhancing sport performance in trained athletes when consumed in low-to-moderate dosages (~3-6 mg/kg) and overall does not result in further enhancement in performance when consumed in higher dosages (>/= 9 mg/kg).

abernethy-1985.title: Impairment of caffeine clearance by chronic use of low-dose oestrogen-containing oral contraceptives
abernethy-1985.support: Treated females matched with 9 non-smoking, drug-free, healthy control females. Each subject received 162 mg caffeine base orally. OCS subjects had a prolonged elimination half-life of caffeine (mean 7.88 h vs 5.37 h in the controls), the result of marked impairment of the plasma clearance of caffeine. With chronic caffeine consumption, OCS users are predicted to have an increased steady-state plasma caffeine concentration.

burdge-2002-men.title: Eicosapentaenoic and docosapentaenoic acids are the principal products of α-linolenic acid metabolism in young men
burdge-2002-men.support: Emulsified [U-13C]ALNA was administered orally with a mixed meal to six subjects. There was no apparent 13C enrichment of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) in plasma PC, TAG or non-esterified fatty acids at any time point measured up to 21 d.

burdge-2002-women.title: Conversion of α-linolenic acid to eicosapentaenoic, docosapentaenoic and docosahexaenoic acids in young women
burdge-2002-women.support: Estimated net fractional ALNA inter-conversion was EPA 21 %, DPA 6 % and DHA 9 %. Comparison with previous studies suggests that women may possess a greater capacity for ALNA conversion than men.

spector-1999.title: Essentiality of fatty acids
spector-1999.support: The need for arachidonic acid ... is the main reason why the n-6 class of PUFA are essential. ... docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is more likely to be the essential n-3 constituent because it is necessary for optimal visual acuity and neural development.

le-2009.title: The essentiality of arachidonic acid and docosahexaenoic acid
le-2009.journal: Prostaglandins, Leukotrienes and Essential Fatty Acids
le-2009.support: No patients receiving PN with a fish oil-based lipid emulsion in our institution have developed biochemical or clinical evidence of EFAD. AA and DHA provision alone is sufficient to prevent biochemical and physiologic evidence of EFAD in a murine model.

demmelmair-1999.title: Comparison of bolus versus fractionated oral applications of [13C]-linoleic acid in humans
demmelmair-1999.support: Oral tracer doses were given to five healthy adults as a single bolus; in four subjects in nine portions. Fractional conversion of linoleic to arachidonic acid was 0.3% vs. 0.6% (bolus vs. fraction, NS).

johnson-2012.title: Effect of Dietary Linoleic Acid on Markers of Inflammation in Healthy Persons: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
johnson-2012.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
johnson-2012.support: Fifteen studies (eight parallel and seven crossover) met inclusion criteria. None of the studies reported significant findings for a wide variety of inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein, fibrinogen, ... cytokines ... or tumor necrosis factor-alpha.

micha-2009.title: Trans fatty acids: effects on metabolic syndrome, heart disease and diabetes
micha-2009.support: Consumption of even small amounts of TFAs (2% of total energy intake) is consistently associated with a markedly increased incidence of coronary heart disease. Relationships between TFA consumption and diabetes mellitus have been less consistent.

shaukat-2010.title: Systematic Review: Effective Management Strategies for Lactose Intolerance
shaukat-2010.support: Moderate-quality evidence indicated that 12 to 15 g of lactose (approximately 1 cup of milk) is well tolerated by most adults. Most studies evaluated persons with lactose malabsorption rather than lactose intolerance.

mcdonald-nutrition-primer.title: A Primer on Nutrition Part 1
mcdonald-nutrition-primer.support: Overview of nutrient classes: the definition of an essential nutrient, carbohydrate as conditionally essential for hard training, fibre giving some energy, and a lower proposed energy value for protein.

mcdonald-carbs-primer.title: A Primer on Dietary Carbohydrates
mcdonald-carbs-primer.support: Sugars, starches and lactose: how lactose intolerance arises from too little lactase and how it differs from a milk allergy.

mcdonald-fats-primer.title: A Primer on Dietary Fats - Part 1
mcdonald-fats-primer.support: Fat classes and the essential fats; his view that trans fat has no place in the diet and that low omega-3 matters more than high omega-6.

mcdonald-real-efa.title: What Are the Real Essential Fatty Acids?
mcdonald-real-efa.support: Essentiality defined; his case that AA and DHA, not LA and ALA, are the truly essential fats, and that ALA is a poor source of EPA and DHA.

kim-2016.title: The anabolic response to a meal containing different amounts of protein is not limited by the maximal stimulation of protein synthesis in healthy young adults
kim-2016.journal: American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism
kim-2016.support: Twenty-three healthy young adults. NB was greater in response to the meal containing HP vs. MP. The greater NB with HP was achieved primarily through a greater reduction in PB and to a lesser extent stimulation of protein synthesis.

smeets-2019.title: Protein synthesis rates of muscle, tendon, ligament, cartilage, and bone tissue in vivo in humans
smeets-2019.support: Six otherwise healthy patients (62±3 y), scheduled to undergo unilateral total knee arthroplasty. Tendon, bone, cartilage, ... cruciate ligament, and menisci tissue protein synthesis rates ... did not significantly differ from skeletal muscle protein synthesis rates (0.04±0.01%/h).

tipton-2004.title: Protein and amino acids for athletes
tipton-2004.support: There are few convincing outcome data to indicate that the ingestion of a high amount of protein (2-3 g/kg BW/day) is necessary. There is limited evidence for harmful effects of a high protein intake.

shams-white-2017.title: Dietary protein and bone health: a systematic review and meta-analysis from the National Osteoporosis Foundation
shams-white-2017.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
shams-white-2017.support: Sixteen RCTs and 20 prospective cohort studies. Higher protein intake may have a protective effect on lumbar spine BMD (net percentage change: 0.52%) but no effect on total hip, femoral neck, or total body BMD. Current evidence shows no adverse effects of higher protein intakes.

gorissen-2018.title: Protein content and amino acid composition of commercially available plant-based protein isolates
gorissen-2018.support: EAA contents of oat (21%), lupin (21%), and wheat (22%) were lower than animal-based proteins (whey 43%, milk 39%, casein 34%, and egg 32%) and muscle protein (38%). Leucine contents ranging from 5.1% for hemp to 13.5% for corn protein, compared to 9.0% for milk, 7.0% for egg, and 7.6% for muscle protein.

gilani-2012.title: Background on international activities on protein quality assessment of foods
gilani-2012.support: The 1991 report concluded that the PDCAAS method was the most suitable approach for routine evaluation of protein quality for humans; the FAO/WHO/UNU (1985) pattern for preschool children was used; the method should be revised to permit values of >100 for high quality proteins.

rutherfurd-2015.title: Protein Digestibility-Corrected Amino Acid Scores and Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Scores Differentially Describe Protein Quality in Growing Male Rats
rutherfurd-2015.support: The FAO has recommended replacing PDCAAS with DIAAS. DIAAS values ranged from 0.01 for a corn-based cereal to 1.18 for milk protein concentrate. Differences in the scores are of potential practical importance for populations in which dietary protein intake may be marginal.

mathai-2017.title: Values for digestible indispensable amino acid scores (DIAAS) for some dairy and plant proteins may better describe protein quality than values calculated using the concept for protein digestibility-corrected amino acid scores (PDCAAS)
mathai-2017.support: PDCAAS-like values were greater than DIAAS values for SMP, PPC, SPI, soya flour and wheat, indicating that PDCAAS-like values estimated in pigs may overestimate the quality of these proteins.

mcdonald-protein-controversies.title: Protein Controversies
mcdonald-protein-controversies.support: Health worries about high protein: why early calcium-loss findings came from purified protein, and his view that adequate calcium plus fruit and vegetables keeps bone safe.

mcdonald-protein-connective.title: Protein Requirements and Connective Tissue
mcdonald-protein-connective.support: Uses a tracer study of connective tissue turnover to argue that protein needs cannot be set from muscle protein synthesis alone.

mcdonald-protein-growth.title: Protein Requirements for Hypertrophy
mcdonald-protein-growth.support: Critique of per-meal protein caps drawn from muscle synthesis studies, and his own daily targets for recreational lifters and high-level strength athletes.

mcdonald-protein-quality-1.title: What Are Good Sources of Protein? - Protein Quality
mcdonald-protein-quality-1.support: Survey of protein quality measures and his view that quality scores matter little for people eating plenty of protein from mixed sources.

boirie-1997.title: Slow and fast dietary proteins differently modulate postprandial protein accretion
boirie-1997.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
boirie-1997.support: WP induced a dramatic but short increase of plasma amino acids. CAS induced a prolonged plateau of moderate hyperaminoacidemia. Whole body protein breakdown was inhibited by 34% after CAS; synthesis stimulated by 68% with WP. Net leucine balance over the 7 h was more positive with CAS.

dangin-2002.title: Influence of the Protein Digestion Rate on Protein Turnover in Young and Elderly Subjects
dangin-2002.support: Our preliminary results suggest that added nonprotein energy sources to CAS and WP attenuated the differences in both the protein digestion rate and protein gain. In contrast to young subjects, a fast protein may be more beneficial than a slow one in elderly subjects.

macnaughton-2016.title: The response of muscle protein synthesis following whole-body resistance exercise is greater following 40 g than 20 g of ingested whey protein
macnaughton-2016.support: Resistance-trained males (lower LBM n = 15, higher LBM n = 15). MPS was stimulated to a greater extent following ingestion of 40 g (0.059%/h) compared with 20 g (0.049%/h); the total amount of LBM does not seem to influence the response.

evenepoel-1998.title: Digestibility of Cooked and Raw Egg Protein in Humans as Assessed by Stable Isotope Techniques
evenepoel-1998.support: Five ileostomy patients; 25 g of cooked or raw egg protein. The true ileal digestibility of cooked and raw egg protein amounted to 90.9 and 51.3%, respectively.

pawlak-2013.title: How prevalent is vitamin B12 deficiency among vegetarians?
pawlak-2013.support: 18 articles; deficiency rates 62% among pregnant women, 25-86% among children, 21-41% among adolescents, 11-90% among the elderly; higher among vegans. Vegetarians should take preventive measures including regular consumption of supplements containing B12.

hurrell-2010.title: Iron bioavailability and dietary reference values
hurrell-2010.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
hurrell-2010.support: Iron bioavailability has been estimated to be in the range of 14-18% for mixed diets and 5-12% for vegetarian diets in subjects with no iron stores. Iron status generally has a greater effect than diet composition.

baer-1997.title: Dietary Fiber Decreases the Metabolizable Energy Content and Nutrient Digestibility of Mixed Diets Fed to Humans
baer-1997.support: Subjects (n = 17) consumed three diets (14 d each). Increasing fiber intake decreased fat and protein digestibility; the ME content of the diets decreased as fiber intake increased.

mcdonald-protein-intro.title: What Are Good Sources of Protein? - Introduction
mcdonald-protein-intro.support: Factors for judging a protein source, and protein digestibility defined as the share of eaten protein that is absorbed.

mcdonald-protein-speed.title: What Are Good Sources of Protein? - Speed of Digestion Pt. 1
mcdonald-protein-speed.support: Fast and slow proteins, the whey and casein studies and their limits, and his preference for a fast protein before or during training.

mcdonald-protein-micronutrients.title: What Are Good Sources of Protein? - Micronutrient Content
mcdonald-protein-micronutrients.support: Iron, zinc, B12 and calcium in protein foods, his case for lean red meat, and his warning against raw egg whites.

mcdonald-post-workout-protein.title: Protein Intake and Post Workout Protein Synthesis
mcdonald-post-workout-protein.support: Review of a study comparing 20 and 40 g of whey after whole-body lifting, with his reading of how large the extra gain was and what the single biopsy site leaves out.

mcdonald-fibre.title: Fiber - Natures Broom
mcdonald-fibre.support: Fibre types and effects, his estimate of the energy lost when fibre is doubled, and his advice on fibre for people who need to eat a lot.

foster-powell-2002.title: International table of glycemic index and glycemic load values: 2002
foster-powell-2002.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
foster-powell-2002.support: chronic consumption of a diet with a high glycemic load (GI x dietary carbohydrate content) ... The revised table also lists the glycemic load associated with the consumption of specified serving sizes of different foods.

mettler-2007.title: The influence of the subjects' training state on the glycemic index
mettler-2007.support: The GI differed significantly between SE and ET subjects (P=0.02, mean difference: 23 GI units ...). The GI of the MT subjects was intermediary ... The insulin index did not differ significantly between the groups.

mettler-2006.title: Influence of Training Status on Glycemic Index
mettler-2006.journal: International Journal for Vitamin and Nutrition Research
mettler-2006.support: Pair-wise comparisons between endurance-trained and sedentary subjects within the different test meals were significant for test meal D (p = 0.002), marginally non-significant for meal C (p = 0.052) and not significant for meal B.

schenk-2003.title: Different glycemic indexes of breakfast cereals are not due to glucose entry into blood but to glucose removal by tissue
schenk-2003.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
schenk-2003.support: Postprandial hyperinsulinemia occurred earlier with BC than with CF, resulting in a 76% higher plasma insulin concentration at 20 min ... The lower GI of BC than of CF was not due to a lower rate of appearance of glucose.

ang-2012.title: Combining protein and carbohydrate increases postprandial insulin levels but does not improve glucose response in patients with type 2 diabetes
ang-2012.support: No significant differences in glucose responses were observed after ingestion of the drinks. Compared to ingestion of ISO alone, insulin response was ~190%-270% higher.

raatz-2005.title: Reduced Glycemic Index and Glycemic Load Diets Do Not Increase the Effects of Energy Restriction on Weight Loss and Insulin Sensitivity in Obese Men and Women
raatz-2005.support: At 12 wk, weight changes from baseline were significant in all groups but not different among groups (-9.3 ... HGI, -9.9 ... LGI, and -8.4 ... HF).

pittas-2005.title: A Low-Glycemic Load Diet Facilitates Greater Weight Loss in Overweight Adults With High Insulin Secretion but Not in Overweight Adults With Low Insulin Secretion in the CALERIE Trial
pittas-2005.support: Brief report with no PubMed abstract; cited only for the finding stated in its title.

jentjens-2003.title: Determinants of Post-Exercise Glycogen Synthesis During Short-Term Recovery
jentjens-2003.support: The highest muscle glycogen synthesis rates have been reported when large amounts of carbohydrate (1.0-1.85 g/kg/h) are consumed immediately post-exercise ... When carbohydrate ingestion is delayed by several hours, this may lead to ~50% lower rates.

hawley-1997.title: Carbohydrate-Loading and Exercise Performance
hawley-1997.support: Nor is there any benefit of increasing starting muscle glycogen content on moderate-intensity running or cycling lasting 60 to 90 minutes ... elevated starting muscle glycogen content will postpone fatigue by approximately 20% in endurance events lasting more than 90 minutes.

fairchild-2002.title: Rapid carbohydrate loading after a short bout of near maximal-intensity exercise
fairchild-2002.support: Muscle glycogen increased from preloading levels of 109.1 +/- 8.2 to 198.2 +/- 13.1 mmol.kg-1 wet weight within only 24 h, these levels being comparable to or higher than those reported by others over a 2- to 6-d regimen.

demoraes-2019.title: Carbohydrate Loading Practice in Bodybuilders: Effects on Muscle Thickness, Photo Silhouette Scores, Mood States and Gastrointestinal Symptoms
demoraes-2019.journal: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
demoraes-2019.support: Body mass, muscle thickness (elbow flexors ... and triceps brachii) and circumferences ... increased significantly in the CL at M2 ... Diarrhea was reported by 7/15 CL (4/15 as severe).

almond-2005.title: Hyponatremia among Runners in the Boston Marathon
almond-2005.support: Thirteen percent had hyponatremia ...; 0.6 percent had critical hyponatremia ... associated with weight gain (odds ratio, 4.2 ...), a racing time of >4:00 hours (odds ratio ... 7.4 ...).

mcdonald-gi-gl.title: A Guide to the Glycemic Index and Glycemic Load
mcdonald-gi-gl.support: How GI is tested and why the 50 g portion misleads, glycaemic load, GI versus insulin, training state, refuelling speed, and his view that lean athletes need not track GI.

mcdonald-carb-loading.title: Carbohydrate Loading for Endurance Events
mcdonald-carb-loading.support: Which events need loading, older and one-day loading plans, total grams over percentages, bodybuilder loading, and overdrinking risk in slower marathoners.

dimeglio-2000.title: Liquid versus solid carbohydrate: effects on food intake and body weight
dimeglio-2000.support: Dietary energy compensation was precise (118%). No decrease in free-feeding energy intake occurred during the liquid period ... body weight and BMI increased significantly only during the liquid period.

wolf-2008.title: A short history of beverages and how our body treats them
wolf-2008.support: beverages containing sugar, high fructose corn syrup (HFCS) or alcohol are handled differently by the body than when sugar or HFCS are incorporated in solid foods ... caloric intake from solid food does not adjust to account for the calories in these beverages.

shirreffs-2007.title: Milk as an effective post-exercise rehydration drink
shirreffs-2007.support: Cumulative urine output was less after the milk drinks (611 and 550 ml ...) compared to 1184 and 1205 ml for the water and sports drink ... Subjects remained in net positive fluid balance or euhydrated throughout the recovery period after drinking the milk drinks.

karp-2006.title: Chocolate Milk as a Post-Exercise Recovery Aid
karp-2006.journal: International Journal of Sport Nutrition and Exercise Metabolism
karp-2006.support: Carbohydrate content was equivalent for chocolate milk and CR ... TTE and WT were significantly greater for chocolate milk and FR trials compared to CR trial.

otun-2019.title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis on the Effect of Soy on Thyroid Function
otun-2019.support: The meta-analysis showed no significant changes in fT3 ... fT4 ... while an elevation in TSH levels was observed (WMD: 0.248 mIU/L ...). Soy supplementation has no effect on the thyroid hormones and only very modestly raises TSH levels.

messina-2006.title: Effects of Soy Protein and Soybean Isoflavones on Thyroid Function in Healthy Adults and Hypothyroid Patients: A Review of the Relevant Literature
messina-2006.support: With only one exception, either no effects or only very modest changes were noted ... soy foods, by inhibiting absorption, may increase the dose of thyroid hormone required by hypothyroid patients. However, hypothyroid adults need not avoid soy foods.

doerge-2002.title: Goitrogenic and estrogenic activity of soy isoflavones
doerge-2002.support: evidence for binding of isoflavones to the estrogen receptor ... Genistein, the major soy isoflavone ... Iodine deficiency greatly increases soy antithyroid effects, whereas iodine supplementation is protective.

reed-2021.title: Neither soy nor isoflavone intake affects male reproductive hormones: An expanded and updated meta-analysis of clinical studies
reed-2021.support: TT and FT levels were measured in 1753 and 752 men ... no significant effects of soy protein or isoflavone intake on any of the outcomes measured ... Sub-analysis of the data according to isoflavone dose and study duration also showed no effect.

ello-martin-2007.title: Dietary energy density in the treatment of obesity: a year-long trial comparing 2 weight-loss diets
ello-martin-2007.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
ello-martin-2007.support: Obese women (n = 97) over 1 y; the group eating more water-rich foods lost 7.9 vs 6.4 kg, ate a greater weight of food at lower energy density and reported less hunger.

mcdonald-energy-density.title: Energy Density
mcdonald-energy-density.support: Defines energy density, shows that water, fibre and processing change it more than fat alone, and argues that dense foods help people who need very high intakes.

mcdonald-beverages.title: A Short History of Beverages and How our Body Treats Them
mcdonald-beverages.support: Review of the Wolf, Bray and Popkin paper: poor compensation for drink calories, the liquid form rather than the sweetener as the problem, and milk as the exception.

mcdonald-milk.title: Milk: The New Sports Drink? A Review
mcdonald-milk.support: Review of milk for strength and endurance athletes: good after training, poor during it, and too small a dose of carbohydrate and protein for large athletes on its own.

mcdonald-soy-thyroid.title: Soy Protein and Phytoestrogens on Thyroid Function
mcdonald-soy-thyroid.support: Soy and thyroid in healthy and hypothyroid people, iodine status, medication timing, isoflavones, and his suggested ceiling on daily soy protein.

white-2008.title: Straight talk about high-fructose corn syrup: what it is and what it ain't
white-2008.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
white-2008.support: It is not meaningfully different in composition or metabolism from other fructose-glucose sweeteners like sucrose, honey, and fruit juice concentrates ... the HFCS-obesity hypothesis is supported neither in the United States nor worldwide.

stanhope-2008.title: Twenty-four-hour endocrine and metabolic profiles following consumption of high-fructose corn syrup-, sucrose-, fructose-, and glucose-sweetened beverages with meals
stanhope-2008.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
stanhope-2008.support: In 34 subjects, 24-h glucose, insulin, leptin, ghrelin, and TG profiles were similar between days that sucrose or HFCS was consumed ... postprandial TG profiles after HFCS or sucrose were ... comparably high as after pure fructose.

livesey-2008.title: Fructose consumption and consequences for glycation, plasma triacylglycerol, and body weight: meta-analyses and meta-regression models of intervention studies
livesey-2008.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
livesey-2008.support: Significant effects on postprandial triacylglycerols are not evident unless >50 g fructose/d is consumed, and no significant effects are seen for fasting triacylglycerol or body weight with intakes of <=100 g fructose/d in adults.

fda-epa-fish.title: Advice about Eating Fish: For Those Who Might Become or Are Pregnant or Breastfeeding and Children Ages 1 to 11 Years
fda-epa-fish.support: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: 1 serving is 4 ounces. Eat 2 to 3 servings a week from the Best Choices list (or 1 serving from the Good Choices list). Choices to avoid (highest mercury): king mackerel, marlin, orange roughy, shark, swordfish, tilefish (Gulf of Mexico), bigeye tuna.

paulsen-2014-endurance.title: Vitamin C and E supplementation hampers cellular adaptation to endurance training in humans: a double-blind, randomised, controlled trial
paulsen-2014-endurance.support: Participants in the vitamin C and E group increased their VO2 max (8 +/- 5%) ... to the same degree as those in the placebo group ... Daily vitamin C and E supplementation attenuated increases in markers of mitochondrial biogenesis following endurance training.

paulsen-2014-strength.title: Vitamin C and E supplementation alters protein signalling after a strength training session, but not muscle growth during 10 weeks of training
paulsen-2014-strength.support: The supplementation did not affect the increase in muscle mass or the acute change in protein synthesis, but it hampered certain strength increases (biceps curl).

bjelakovic-2012.title: Antioxidant supplements for prevention of mortality in healthy participants and patients with various diseases
bjelakovic-2012.support: In the 56 trials with a low risk of bias, the antioxidant supplements significantly increased mortality (RR 1.04) ... Beta-carotene and vitamin E seem to increase mortality, and so may higher doses of vitamin A.

farrokhyar-2015.title: Prevalence of Vitamin D Inadequacy in Athletes: A Systematic-Review and Meta-Analysis
farrokhyar-2015.support: Of 2,313 athletes, 56 % had vitamin D inadequacy [serum 25(OH)D <32 ng/mL] ... The risk significantly increased for winter and spring seasons ..., indoor sport activities ... its association with vitamin D status is unclear.

ross-2011.title: The 2011 Report on Dietary Reference Intakes for Calcium and Vitamin D from the Institute of Medicine: What Clinicians Need to Know
ross-2011.journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
ross-2011.support: For vitamin D, RDAs of 600 IU/d for ages 1-70 yr and 800 IU/d for ages 71 yr and older, corresponding to a serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level of at least 20 ng/ml ... Higher values were not consistently associated with greater benefit ... prevalence of vitamin D inadequacy in North America has been overestimated.

candow-2001.title: Effect of glutamine supplementation combined with resistance training in young adults
candow-2001.support: glutamine (0.9 g x kg lean tissue mass-1 x day-1) ... Both groups increased their 1 RM squat by approximately 30% and 1 RM bench press by approximately 14% ... no significant effect on muscle performance, body composition or muscle protein degradation.

mcdonald-hfcs.title: High-fructose corn syrup: what it is and what it ain't.
mcdonald-hfcs.support: Review of White's paper: HFCS composition against sucrose, correlation with obesity, pure-fructose studies, and his view that the calories and soft drinks are the issue.

mcdonald-fructose-diet.title: The Effect of a Low- or High-fructose diet on Weight Loss
mcdonald-fructose-diet.support: Background on fructose intakes, his 50 g a day figure for the liver, unrealistic doses in feeding studies, and fruit in a fat-loss diet.

mcdonald-mercury.title: Fish Intake and Mercury
mcdonald-mercury.support: Mercury in common fish, pregnancy, and his warning that heavy daily tuna eaters can exceed reference limits.

mcdonald-antioxidant-vitd.title: Antioxidant and Vitamin D Supplements for Athletes
mcdonald-antioxidant-vitd.support: Review of the case for and against antioxidant and vitamin D supplements in athletes, with his views on training blocks, competition seasons and indoor athletes.

mcdonald-supplements-1.title: Supplements Part 1
mcdonald-supplements-1.support: Book chapter ranking supplements for mixed-sport athletes, including his views on antioxidants, vitamin D, glutamine and BCAA.

atherton-2010.title: Muscle full effect after oral protein: time-dependent concordance and discordance between human muscle protein synthesis and mTORC1 signaling
atherton-2010.journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
atherton-2010.support: At 45-90 min after oral protein bolus, myofibrillar protein synthesis increased ...; thereafter, myofibrillar protein synthesis returned to baseline rates even though plasma essential AA concentrations remained elevated.

areta-2013.title: Timing and distribution of protein ingestion during prolonged recovery from resistance exercise alters myofibrillar protein synthesis
areta-2013.support: 80 g of whey protein throughout 12 h recovery ... 8 x 10 g every 1.5 h; 4 x 20 g every 3 h; or 2 x 40 g every 6 h ... INT elicited greater MPS than PULSE and BOLUS (31-48%).

res-2012.title: Protein Ingestion before Sleep Improves Postexercise Overnight Recovery
res-2012.support: Protein ingestion before sleep increased whole-body protein synthesis rates ... and improved net protein balance ... Mixed muscle protein synthesis rates were ~22% higher ..., which reached borderline significance (P = 0.05).

garthe-2013.title: Effect of nutritional intervention on body composition and performance in elite athletes
garthe-2013.support: Energy intake was higher in the NCG than in the ALG (3585 vs. 2964 kcal) ... BW increased more in NCG than in ALG (3.9 vs. 1.5%). Fat mass increased more in NCG than in ALG (15 vs 3%), but gain in LBM was not different between groups.

mcdonald-calories-gain.title: Determining Calorie Intake for Muscle Gain
mcdonald-calories-gain.support: Works out how small a surplus realistic muscle gain needs at each training stage, and argues that larger surpluses mostly add fat.

mcdonald-meal-freq-mass.title: Meal Frequency for Mass Gains
mcdonald-meal-freq-mass.support: Book excerpt on the muscle-full research and his case for meals three to five hours apart when gaining.

mcdonald-baseline.title: The Baseline Diet: Part 1
mcdonald-baseline.support: His starting template for lifters: meal spacing, eating before bed, adjusting a gaining surplus by skinfolds, fluids and macronutrients.

mcdonald-carb-needs.title: How Many Carbohydrates Do You Need
mcdonald-carb-needs.support: Carbohydrate needs from zero upward, where ketosis begins, and the limits of urine ketone strips.

mcdonald-keto-ratio.title: Ketosis and The Ketogenic Ratio - Q&A
mcdonald-keto-ratio.support: Why he dropped the ketogenic ratio for fat-loss diets, ketosis as a result of fat burning, and why urine strips mislead.
